value.title: Conditional-product and correlation-structure pruning
value.summary: Determine which coordinate-packet factorizations preclude multiletter Marton gains and derive decomposition-relative correlation constraints that any remaining nonproduct witness must satisfy.

value.title: Receiver-skew Marton midpoint identity
value.summary: Reflecting a Marton law exchanges the two receivers and the U,V roles, making the associated affine supremum symmetric about weight one half. A tagged mixture of a law and its reflection proves directly, without an attainment or minimax assumption, that the private-message Marton supremum equals the half-weight affine supremum for every finite receiver-skew channel.

value.title: Conditional-product Marton tensorization proof
value.summary: Conditioning on the arbitrary common auxiliary makes the coordinate satellite-input packets independent. The three conditional Marton terms then add exactly, while each common-receiver information term is subadditive across coordinates. The receiver-skew midpoint identity bounds every coordinate marginal by the one-letter Marton value; independent epsilon-optimal copies give the reverse inequality, proving exact n-fold scaling without an attainment assumption.

value.title: Tuple-decomposition correlation residual identity
value.summary: For an arbitrary finite tuple law followed by the product channel, entropy expansion expresses the difference between the aggregate half-weight Marton functional and the sum of its coordinate marginals as an exact combination of conditional total correlations and cross-conditioning gaps. Combining this identity with the receiver-skew midpoint bound yields the strict correlation-balance inequality required by any strict multiletter gain for the chosen decomposition. Constant padding ensures a tuple representation exists, but the ledger is decomposition dependent.

value.title: Conditional-product and correlation-ledger verifier
value.summary: A deterministic standard-library script checks the exact half-skew BSSC receiver relabeling and, on fixed-seed finite examples, corroborates conditional-product entropy additivity, common-term subadditivity, independent-copy Marton equality, the exact correlated-tuple residual identity, nonnegativity of its displayed components, and the symmetric forms of the penalty term. These finite checks support but do not replace the universal analytic proofs.

value.title: Conditional-product Marton no-gain theorem
value.summary: For every finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channel and every n≥1, the n-letter Marton supremum restricted to coordinate satellite-input packets that are independent conditional on an arbitrary common W equals n times the one-letter private-message Marton value. Thus any strict two-letter half-skew BSSC gain must fail every tested conditional-product packet decomposition. For arbitrary tuple laws, the exact decomposition-relative total-correlation residual identity holds and any strict gain must satisfy its strict correlation-balance inequality. This establishes neither unrestricted Marton additivity nor a capacity bound or exact BSSC capacity.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted theorem directly advances the active multiletter Marton objective by excluding a broad conditional-product architecture and supplying correlation-based pruning conditions for the remaining nonproduct search.
